subject: Exec Pulse: OKR micro-checks, QBR evidence requests, and three strategic asks
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Exec Pulse: OKR micro-checks, QBR evidence requests, and three strategic asks

Team —

Quick weekly pulse as we lock the QBR pack next week. I kept this tight on purpose (TL;DR at the top).

TL;DR
- Wins: Hosted API latency 95p improved by 12% vs last week; Dedicated capacity pilot hit SLA for first week.
- Risks: 1) Small but growing model-serving throttle during long-context traces (affects a few high-throughput customers). 2) QBR evidence gaps for SOC-2 artifacts and the cost-per-token analysis.
- Asks: See three targeted asks at the bottom.

Wins (brief)
- Hosted API: End-to-end 95th latency down from 420ms -> 370ms after the kernel swap and reduced batch window (metrics from 05/24-05/29). This is the immediate runtime win Sasha and infra team shipped.
- Dedicated: Pilot cluster for Acme Analytics (reserved-nyc-1) sustained 120 tps with sub-150ms p50 for short-gen tests; customer reported no timeout errors during integration smoke.
- Observability: Console rollout to beta customers shows token-level cost attribution in prod for two routes (alpha). Early feedback: very useful for cost debugging.

Risks / Items to watch
1) Long-context throughput degradation: We still see KV-cache eviction storms when sequence lengths spike above 8k for a small subset (~2%) of requests — this is causing transient throttle behavior. Root cause looks like cache fragmentation + batching decisions. Engineering is on a fast path but needs time and load tests.
2) QBR evidence gaps: We are missing two artifacts for the QBR pack: a) SOC-2 evidence index (log retention policy snapshots) and b) detailed cost-per-100k-token breakdown for Hosted vs Dedicated for our top 5 customers.
3) Commercial: Acme Analytics may ask for a short-term credit if we cannot certify the Dedicated SLA for a committed roll-in next month. I flagged this to AE (Maria) and CS; we should be prepared to authorize up to 10k in credits as an exec-level decision if needed.

Three targeted asks (concrete)
A) Security/compliance: Laura — can you have Compliance produce a one-page SOC-2 evidence index by EOD Wed (05/31)? I attached the current inventory with highlights where evidence is missing.
B) Cost analysis: Vivek — please prioritize a short table comparing unit cost (per 100k tokens) Hosted vs Dedicated for the top-5 accounts by revenue. We need this for the QBR slide showing cost delta and margin impact; a single slide is fine.
C) Tactical mitigation: Markus — can Engineering provide a short mitigation plan (3 bullets + ETA) for the long-context throttle by Tue 6/1? If we can get a patch to reduce KV eviction within 5 business days, we avoid escalation with Acme.

Attachments: qbr_evidence_inventory.xlsx (inventory + flagged gaps), okr-micro-checks-heatmap.pdf (team-level OKR micro-check visualization).

Notes on OKR micro-checks
- Platform stability: On track overall (green) but long-context metric is amber.
- Performance: p95 latency target is improving; keep eyes on memory/batching trade-offs.
- Go-to-market: Sales pipeline shows a +15% MRR delta where cost is the gating factor — this is why the cost slide matters for the QBR.

Next steps: short follow-ups expected from each of you. If we can close A/B/C by Tue/Wed cadence we avoid raising to the board level.

Thanks —
Karthik
Karthik Iyer | VP, Platform Partnerships | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1-415-555-0192

Subject: Re: Exec Pulse: OKR micro-checks, QBR evidence requests, and three strategic asks

Thanks Karthik — clean summary. A couple quick notes: 

- On SOC-2 evidence: I'll ask Compliance to prioritize the index; they should be able to produce the index document by Wed EOD but will need the exact list of artifacts you flagged. Please mark items in the inventory file where you want a copy of the supporting docs (logs, configs, retention policy).
- QBR slide ask: fine — I can own producing a single slide for SOC & evidence status if you (Vivek) can drop the cost numbers into the same doc. That keeps the pack small and focused.

One operational ask: for the Acme credit possibility, let's not pre-authorize without seeing the mitigation ETA. If Engineering can hit the 5-business-day patch, we should avoid moving dollars.

Laura Bennett
Chief of Staff, GTM Operations | Redwood Inference

Appreciate the crisp note. Two quick clarifications and a request: 

1) Cost table scope: When you say "top-5 customers by revenue" — do you want them ranked by ARR or by token spend? For the QBR margin narrative I prefer ARR, but token spend shows unit economics more clearly. Recommend ARR primary, token-spend as a supplemental column.
2) Acme credit: understood on the pause — but can we set a guardrail now? If Engineering's ETA goes beyond 7 business days I want the option to approve a credit up to 5k immediately to keep the account in momentum while we patch. That keeps sales from stalling.

Request: Can someone (Karthik/Markus) add a short table row in the drive folder with the last 30-day token counts for Acme's production routes? That will help quantify the cost delta and inform the credit decision.

Thanks —
Vivek
Head of Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
